agency.name: Verkehrsverbund Berlin-Brandenburg (VBB)
agency.operating_note: One multi-operator regional aggregate for Berlin and Brandenburg; counted as one feed record, not a distinct-agency count. The publisher's GTFS-Flex collection is reviewed as a separate demand-responsive feed.

findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
findings.what: 38884 of 42078 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
findings.what: 34118 of 244363 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
findings.why: Even with accessible stops, riders need to know the transit vehicle itself can take them.

findings.effort: A small file for most flat-fare systems.
findings.fix: Add fare_attributes.txt (or Fares v2 files) with your fare structure. If your service is fare-free, ask to have it marked fare-free instead.
findings.what: The feed contains no fare information.
findings.why: Riders see 'fare unknown' in trip planners and can't budget their trip; visitors are most affected.

findings.effort: Usually one value per route pattern in your scheduling source.
findings.fix: Add the destination, direction, or 'via' label riders actually see to trip_headsign. Do not copy the route name. If the label changes during the trip, use stop_headsign.
findings.what: 42 of 244363 trips lack rider-facing destination or direction text.
findings.why: When a route has multiple directions or patterns, the route name alone may not tell riders which service is coming.

findings.effort: One field.
findings.fix: Add feed_contact_email to feed_info.txt.
findings.what: feed_info.txt has no technical contact (feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url).
findings.why: Trip-planning apps and regional data coordinators have nobody to email when they spot a problem with your feed, so problems linger.

findings.effort: None.
findings.fix: No action needed.
findings.what: This feed describes station pathways, including step-free (elevator) routes.
findings.why: Riders can be routed through the station, and wheelchair users can see whether a step-free route exists.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 8% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (8% marked accessible, 0% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is not published.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'block_trips_with_overlapping_stop_times' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Block trips with overlapping stop times (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A planned ID change, not a quick text cleanup.
findings.fix: Only change the flagged IDs if an app needs basic ASCII values. Update each place that uses the ID. Keep all names and headsigns in their original language.
findings.what: Some internal IDs use characters outside the basic text set.
findings.why: These IDs are valid UTF-8 data. This warning is only about support in older apps. It does not mean that names in other languages are wrong.

findings.effort: A review pass in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Remove retired stops from the export, or add them back to the trips that should serve them.
findings.what: Some stops exist in the feed but no trip ever stops at them.
findings.why: Riders may walk to a stop where no transit vehicle is scheduled to arrive.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'unexpected_enum_value' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Unexpected enum value (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A few minutes in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Delete the empty calendars or set their service days.
findings.what: Some service calendars have no days of the week switched on.
findings.why: Trips tied to these calendars never run; they are dead data that can mask real schedule problems.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged stop.
findings.fix: Check the flagged stops' coordinates and the route shape in your scheduling software; re-snap whichever is misplaced.
findings.what: Some stops sit far from the route line they belong to.
findings.why: Trip planners may draw the transit vehicle route through the wrong path or point riders to the wrong boarding location.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged trip.
findings.fix: Check the flagged stop times for transposed minutes.
findings.what: Some scheduled trips move faster between stops than a transit vehicle can.
findings.why: Usually a typo'd stop time; riders get arrival times no transit vehicle can meet.

findings.effort: One field per route.
findings.fix: Give each route a distinct short or long name.
findings.what: Two or more routes share the same name.
findings.why: Riders can't tell the routes apart in apps.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'pathway_dangling_generic_node' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Pathway dangling generic node (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'same_name_and_description_for_stop' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Same name and description for stop (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Use mixed case for stop names and headsigns (e.g. 'Main St & 2nd Ave', not 'MAIN ST & 2ND AVE').
findings.what: Some rider-facing names are in ALL CAPS or all lowercase.
findings.why: ALL-CAPS stop and headsign names are harder to read in apps and are read awkwardly by screen readers.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged trip.
findings.fix: Check the stop order and the shape direction in your scheduling software; the shape is often drawn backwards.
findings.what: On some trips the stops fall along the route line in a different order than the schedule lists.
findings.why: Trip planners can draw the transit vehicle doubling back or skipping ahead, which confuses riders reading the map.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'inconsistent_route_type_for_block_id' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Inconsistent route type for block id (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: One setting in most export tools.
findings.fix: Remove past service periods the next time you export the feed.
findings.what: Some service calendars in the feed have already ended.
findings.why: Expired calendars are dead weight and can hide real schedule problems from your staff and vendors.

findings.effort: One small file, set once in export settings.
findings.fix: Add feed_info.txt with publisher name, URL, language, and feed_start_date/feed_end_date.
findings.what: A file GTFS asks for (usually feed_info.txt) is missing.
findings.why: feed_info.txt tells apps who publishes the feed and when it expires; without it nobody is warned before data goes stale.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'platform_without_parent_station' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Platform without parent station (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A review of your calendar dates.
findings.fix: Check whether the gap is real, like a seasonal break; if not, add the missing dates to the calendar.
findings.what: The feed has a stretch of two weeks or more with no service running.
findings.why: A long gap can mean dates were left out of the calendar. Apps then show no trips on those days.

findings.effort: Varies.
findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'transfer_distance_above_2_km' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Transfer distance above 2 km (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

correctness.name: correctness
correctness.summary: The MobilityData validator flagged 18 kinds of issue across 11900 instances (3 error, 11203 warning, 694 informational).

findings.effort: Two fields, set once in export settings.
findings.fix: Add feed_info.txt with feed_start_date and feed_end_date to your export.
findings.what: feed_info.txt is missing its start/end dates (the file itself is absent)
findings.why: Apps and this scorecard can't warn anyone before the feed goes stale without stated validity dates.

freshness.summary: Service data covers the next 127 days.

conformance.summary: This feed is close to the conformance mark. 1 validator error to resolve. States wheelchair access on 8% of stops and 86% of trips; the mark needs 90% of each.

recommendations.effort: A per-route color setting in your scheduling software.
recommendations.fix: Adjust route_color or route_text_color so each pair clears 4.5:1. Often switching the text between black and white is enough.
recommendations.what: 57 route badge(s) pair a color and text color below the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast bar (RB60, RB54, RB54, RB35, RB26, and more).
recommendations.why: Low-contrast route badges are hard to read for riders with low vision and wash out on a phone screen in sunlight at the stop.

recommendations.effort: A short text field per affected stop; start with the busiest.
recommendations.fix: Add tts_stop_name with the spoken form, e.g. 'Main Street and Second Avenue', for the affected stops.
recommendations.what: 5419 stop name(s) use abbreviations or symbols a screen reader may mispronounce, with no spoken form set ("S+U Lichtenberg Bhf (Berlin)", "S+U Lichtenberg Bhf (Berlin)", "S+U Lichtenberg Bhf (Berlin)", and more).
recommendations.why: Riders who use a screen reader hear the raw name, so 'Main St & 2nd Ave' can come out as 'Main saint' or drop the ampersand.

findings.effort: A cleanup pass in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Remove stops no route serves, or add the trips that should call at them.
findings.what: 1435 of 27992 boardable stops are never served by any trip.
findings.why: Riders see these stops in apps and on the map but can never catch anything there, which erodes trust in the data.
